question: The income of Raman is ₹80,200. He saves 7.5% of his income. If his income increases by 34% and expenditure increases by 40%, then his savings will:
solution:
**Given:**

Income of Raman = ₹80,200

Savings percentage = 7.5%

Income increase = 34%

Expenditure increase = 40%

**Formula Used:**

Savings = Income × Savings percentage

Expenditure = Income - Savings

New Income = Income × (1 + Income increase percentage)

New Expenditure = Expenditure × (1 + Expenditure increase percentage)

New Savings = New Income - New Expenditure

**Calculation:**

⇒ Savings = ₹80,200 × 7.5% = ₹80,200 × 7.5 ÷ 100 = ₹6,015

⇒ Expenditure = ₹80,200 - ₹6,015 = ₹74,185

⇒ New Income = ₹80,200 × (1 + 34%) = ₹80,200 × 1.34 = ₹1,07,468

⇒ New Expenditure = ₹74,185 × (1 + 40%) = ₹74,185 × 1.4 = ₹1,03,859

⇒ New Savings = ₹1,07,468 - ₹1,03,859 = ₹3,609

⇒ Change in Savings = New Savings - Old Savings = ₹3,609 - ₹6,015 = -₹2,406

**∴ The correct answer is decrease by ₹2,406.**
